title: Get an Over-the-Counter permit for your interior residential remodel

paragraphs: Step-by-step
Follow these instructions for projects like kitchen, bath, and other interior residential remodels.
The Department of Building Inspection reviews every building permit application for life safety and building code compliance.
Most interior residential remodels can be reviewed Over-the-Counter (OTC) . Review our instructions to prepare the right forms and book a time to submit your building permit application.
If you are a registered contractor, you can apply through the PermitSF portal for in-kind, non-structural kitchen and bath remodeling that does not require plans.
If your interior residential project is not eligible for OTC review, follow the steps for in-house review .

sections.heading: Check where to apply for your permit
paragraphs: Ways to apply for a permit
The City offers multiple ways to apply for a permit, including the PermitSF Portal, Online Contractor Permits, Over-the-Counter, and In-House Review.
See a list of which permit types are available for each way to apply
Identify your permit type and how to apply
Choose the option below that applies to your project.
If your permit type is available in the PermitSF Portal, create a free OpenGov account to apply for a permit and track its status.
If your permit type is available as an Online Contractor Permit, apply through our online system .
If your permit type is available Over-the-Counter, apply in person at the Permit Center .
If your permit requires In-House Review, submit your application for plan review .
Licensed contractors
For PermitSF Portal applications, verify your license and add any authorized agents to your license before applying. Learn how to register yourself or authorized agents in the PermitSF Portal .
For Online Contractor Permits, Over-the-Counter, or In-House Review, register with the City as a licensed contractor before applying.

sections.heading: Check if your project qualifies for Over-the-Counter
paragraphs: These interior residential projects qualify for Over-the-Counter review:
Interior remodels
Kitchen or bathroom remodels that require plans for R-3 residential buildings
Kitchen or bathroom remodels in R-2 apartment buildings constructed after 1991
New bathrooms
New laundry rooms
Repairing decks and stairs (less than 50%)

sections.heading: Confirm you have a valid address
paragraphs: Confirm your building address using the San Francisco Property Information Map (SFPIM).
Type in your address in the top search bar to confirm the address where construction will occur.
If your address does not come up, you will need to request a new address and pay a fee to create the a new address.

sections.heading: Check if your project needs plans
paragraphs: You need plans for a:
Kitchen remodel (changing layout, floor plan or removing walls)
Bathroom remodel (changing layout, floor plan or removing walls)
Residential interior remodel (changing floor plans or removing walls)
Structural repairs and alterations
Voluntary seismic upgrade
New mechanical equipment installed inside or outside the building (when a building permit is required)
New laundry center, washer, dryer, or laundry sink hookups in new/existing areas within the existing building
In-kind replacement of garage slab (no ceiling height changes) Note: saw-cutting SOG to repair/replace sewer lines does not require plans
Brace and bolt seismic upgrade per DBI Information Sheet S-09
Projects that do not require Planning Department neighborhood notifications
Hire a designer, architect, or engineer to prepare your plans.
Create your building project plans
Bring two sets of plans when you submit your building permit application.
Email techq@sfgov.org if you are not sure if your project needs plans.

sections.heading: Check if your project needs seismic work
paragraphs: Your construction project may require earthquake safety improvements if it includes any of these:
Horizontal addition that adds more than 30% to the size in square feet of the building
Structural alterations to more than 30% of the floor and roof areas
Changes to walls and ceilings on more two-thirds of the stories of the building
Change of occupancy of more than 100 people
Adding 3rd dwelling unit in a below-ground basement
Hire an engineer to work with your architect.

sections.heading: Fill out forms about your role on the project
paragraphs: We need to know your role on the project to apply for an OTC permit.
See: Who can obtain a building permit
Pick the form that applies to you.
For owners, fill out the owner package.

For contractors, fill out the contractor statement. Contractors using the PermitSF digital portal can sign up for contractor authorization and add authorized employees to obtain permits on their behalf.
Print them and bring them with you when apply for a building permit.

sections.heading: Fill out the building form
paragraphs: You will need property and construction details to fill out the building permit application.

sections.heading: Fill out the Green Building form
paragraphs: All building permit applications must fill out our Green Building forms.

sections.heading: Fill out water use forms
paragraphs: For construction projects that add new water fixtures or fire sprinklers, fill out this form.

sections.heading: Submit your application
paragraphs: Come to the Permit Center to submit your application.
If your project needs plans, bring two sets of plans when you submit your building permit application.
You will get a building permit application number.
We will review your application, check your plans, and route your application to the required stations in person.
You may need to come back on a separate day to finish your plans.
Please note that the Department of Building Inspection (DBI) is now conducting all disabled access review as part of our plan review.
Plans requiring a DBI permit that are not project managed by the Department of Public Works no longer need to go to Mayor’s Office on Disability (MOD) for accessibility review and inspection.
Projects that began with MOD and remain unapproved will stay with the same plan checker at DBI or will be reassigned accordingly. Please refer to MOD's website for additional information.

Homeowners may obtain a confidential third-party code inspection from a licensed contractor to determine the unit’s existing condition or potential scope of building improvements before submitting an application for a permit.

sections.heading: Recheck your plans
paragraphs: You may need to update your plans to address plan check comments.
After you address plan check comments, recheck your plans with the plan checker from your first review. Schedule with your plan checker by email.

sections.heading: Get related permits
paragraphs: During your permit review process, you may also need to:
Get a street space permit
Apply for trades permits
For registered contractors, apply for electrical and plumbing permits through the PermitSF portal.
Note: Electrical & Plumbing work must have permits separate from the building permit.

sections.heading: Pay your remaining fees and get your job card
paragraphs: 3 to 4.5% of construction cost
You must have your job card before you can start construction.
See what to bring to get your job card for an issued permit.
Post your construction document at the construction site.
